extracted.intended_audience: middle-level mathematics teachers enrolled in the Math in the Middle Institute and instructors/assistants running these courses
extracted.subtask_description: Syllabus and instructor notes for Math 804T: Experimentation, Conjecture, and Reasoning (a professional-development course for middle-level teachers). Describes course goals, session structure, assessments, grading, materials, instructor/assistant duties, and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Objectives / Mathematical Habits of Mind
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal for this course is to bring you to a new level of your mathematical habits of mind. A productive mathematical thinker has skills and knowledge to experiment, conjecture, reason, and solve problems. 'Mathematical habits of mind' means understanding and using the skills and knowledge. Mathematical habits of mind are marked by flexibility of thinking and the belief that precise exposition of solutions is important. Flexibility of thinking includes using indirect arguments and making connections between knowledge the mathematical thinker possesses and the problem being considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed behaviors: collect information, assess it, find multiple pathways to the answer, explain solutions to others, know why algorithms work and when they'll be effective, ease of calculation and estimation, persistence, analyze all situations, self-efficacy to make progress, and engage in metacognition (monitoring and reflecting on reasoning, conjecturing, proving, problem solving).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment to 'Adding It Up' five strands
rubrics_metrics.description: Course objectives are consistent with the five strands from Adding It Up: 1. Conceptual Understanding 2. Adaptive Reasoning 3. Procedural Fluency 4. Mathematical Problem Solving Competence 5. Productive Disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these strands as lenses for designing activities and assessing whether participants develop mathematical habits of mind; consult [12] for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment to NCTM Principles and Standards processes
rubrics_metrics.description: From the Principles and Standards for School Mathematics, the course focuses on: 1. Problem Solving 2. Reasoning and Proof 3. Communication 4. Connections 5. Representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame course activities and assessments (especially reasoning and exposition tasks) to develop these processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Session activity pattern (sub-session workflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: In each sub-session you will have a pattern of activities: 1) Read the textbook section to prepare; 2) Complete a Pre-Test (five AMC problems) — diagnostic and ungraded; 3) Complete five assigned 'Solidifying Ideas' problems and submit for grading; 4) Complete two 'New Ideas' problems and submit solutions; 5) Complete the assigned 'Habits of Mind' problem and submit; 6) Complete a Post-Test (five AMC problems) and write Session Reflections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-Test is drawn from same database as Pre-Test; Session Reflections ask for a one-page reflection on one problem from each major session and how it was used/shared in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of assigned problems per sub-session
rubrics_metrics.description: Each approximately week-long sub-section assigns eight problems: five from 'Solidifying Ideas', two from 'New Ideas', and one 'Habits of Mind' problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solidifying Ideas exercise calculation/estimation and persistence; New Ideas develop disposition and analytic skills; Habits of Mind problems exercise flexibility and connections. Solutions are submitted weekly and included in the portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Test / Post-Test policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pre-Test consists of five mathematics problems drawn from prior AMC contest problems relevant to the sub-session and is not for grading (diagnostic). The Post-Test consists of five AMC problems drawn from the same database and measures progress; students may take the Post-Test until they reach mastery of the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-Test assesses where students start; Post-Test allows multiple attempts for mastery — intended to measure growth in mathematical habits of mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homework problem scoring rubric and per-sub-session scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the 10 or 11 sub-sessions has eight problems that will be graded on a scale of '1' for a good or satisfactory solution, '2' for a better or noteworthy solution, and '3' for an excellent or exemplary solution. Therefore each sub-session will be worth up to 24 points total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homework scores roll into course grade: each homework sub-session counts for 5% of the course grade (totaling ~50%). Instructors will offer comments to assist improvement; a personalized grade letter at course end is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course-grade weight distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Grading will be based on the work submitted for the Portfolio, the weekly Solidifying Ideas/New Ideas/Habits of Mind solutions, the Post-Tests, and the Essays on Proof. Specific weights: homework sub-sessions ~50% (each ~5%), the seven Post-Tests about 25% total (~3.5% each), the Learning and Teaching Project and the End-of-Course Problem set ~10%, and Blackboard discussion responses/critiques ~5%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this distribution to prioritize tasks; instructors value demonstration of effort, teamwork, progress, and development of knowledge/skills/dispositions for teaching and inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading philosophy and expectations (professionalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect a well-defined sense of professionalism: give assignments your best effort, develop responsibility to your educational community, exhibit persistent desire to learn. The assessment system values effort, teamwork, progress in learning mathematics, and development of knowledge, skills, and dispositions for teaching and inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged behaviors include active participation, on-time submission, supportive interaction with peers, and seeking instructor assistance as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grade-level descriptors and expectations (AC, A, A-, BC, B, B-)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations and typical characteristics of achievement at each grade level are described: AC is honorary and rare — evidence of special admiration (achievement beyond A); A (and variants) show good/very good command of mathematics studied, ability to transfer to classroom, and progress in knowledge/skills/dispositions; BC/B/B- describe decreasing levels of attendance, participation, timeliness, cooperation, and effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these descriptors to interpret numerical/qualitative performance: attendance, participation, timely submission, cooperation, and evidence of learning and progress influence grade bands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late homework and re-do policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Homework should be faxed to the Center Office on the due date. Any problem on which you receive a grade of '1' can be re-done and resubmitted up to one week after the homework is returned for a re-grade. Contact instructors for special consideration if late submission is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy prioritizes learning over punitive grading; communicate proactively for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio and binder expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: You will include submitted homework solutions in a three-ring binder (divided by section) as your portfolio. The Learning and Teaching Project materials and selected homework solutions are included in the portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolios preserve work and provide evidence of progress; include reflections on what is clear and confusing; you may keep all work or only final solutions for problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching and Learning Project (LTP) assignment and assessment reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching and Learning Project explores using course mathematics in the classroom and the relation between understanding and teaching effectiveness. For this semester everyone should use problems 6 (Baby Bunnies) and 9 (Late Bloomers) as the basis for the lesson. Materials turned in for the LTP 'will be assessed according to the rubric outlined on the pages labeled "Assessment Rubric for Written Reflections on Learning and Teaching Project" in your portfolio.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt problems for chosen student age/level, decide starting point and expected outcomes, and include reflections and evidence of classroom implementation. The specific assessment rubric is in the portfolio pages referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for weekly Essays on Proof and communication expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading and writing serve as a basis for some learning. When asked to read or write you are expected to: read so you can be an active participant in discussions, and write so you can respond to posed questions clearly and grammatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students found writing about mathematical ideas (Essays on Proof) challenging; instructors will offer comments to improve exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant instructor duties and support requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Duties for assistant instructors included: answering daily Blackboard questions, leading small-group problem sessions (in person or remotely), grading weekly homework and providing feedback, assisting with creating problems for end-of-course problem set, weekly essays, MapleTA problem databases, and writing/distributing detailed solutions to weekly problem sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide assistant instructors with Instructor's Manual and solutions prior to course start; assistants help sustain contact in distance education settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required materials, manipulatives and technology for workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: For the beginning workshop and course activities provide: VCR (for videos), cardstock, scissors, rulers, manipulatives included with the course kit (straws and pipe cleaners, card triangle kit, etc.), TI-84 calculator and projection system, computer with projection to demonstrate course web-pages and MapleTA, and access to a computer lab with Internet and MapleTA login info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials support hands-on experimentation (students liked manipulatives); ensure logistics for distance students (login info, lab access) are arranged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course prerequisites and required text
rubrics_metrics.description: Prerequisites: Math 800T or Math 802T in the Math in the Middle Program or equivalent. Required Text: The Heart of Mathematics, Second Edition, by E. Burger and M. Starbird (2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructors may supplement text where background facts are missing; post review materials on course website as needed.
